name: @kitora/pickers
description: Kitora's date, time and colour pickers: typed-segment date and time fields, calendars (single, multiple, range), range presets, month, year, week and quarter pickers, datetime, a time-zone picker, an RRULE recurrence editor, a colour picker and an emoji picker, on a framework-free core with Intl locales and RTL.

exports.name: clamp
exports.description: Clamps `n` into `[min, max]`.
exports.signature: (n: number, min: number, max: number) => number

exports.name: COLOR_FORMATS
exports.description: The three text formats the inputs can show and `formatColor` can write.

exports.name: WCAG_AA
exports.description: WCAG 2 contrast thresholds: AA body text, AA large text / UI, AAA body text.

exports.name: WCAG_AA_LARGE
exports.description: WCAG 2 AA contrast threshold for large text and UI parts.

exports.name: WCAG_AAA
exports.description: WCAG 2 AAA contrast threshold for body text.

exports.name: compositeOver
exports.description: `top` painted over `bottom` (alpha blending); the result is opaque when `bottom` is.

exports.name: contrastRatio
exports.description: WCAG 2 contrast ratio between two colours, 1–21.

exports.name: formatColor
exports.description: Writes `rgba` in the chosen format.

exports.name: formatHex
exports.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` only when `a < 1`.
exports.signature: ({ r, g, b, a }: Rgba) => string

exports.name: formatHsl
exports.description: `hsl(h s% l%)`, or with `/ a` when not opaque; numbers rounded to whole degrees and percents.
exports.signature: ({ h, s, l, a }: Hsla) => string

exports.name: formatRgb
exports.description: `rgb(r g b)`, or `rgb(r g b / a)` when not opaque (CSS Color 4 space syntax).
exports.signature: ({ r, g, b, a }: Rgba) => string

exports.name: hslaToHsva
exports.description: HSL → HSV without going through RGB, so the hue survives.
exports.signature: ({ h, s, l, a }: Hsla) => Hsva

exports.name: hslaToRgba
exports.description: HSL → RGB (via HSV).

exports.name: hsvaToHsla
exports.description: HSV → HSL without going through RGB, so the hue survives.
exports.signature: ({ h, s, v, a }: Hsva) => Hsla

exports.name: hsvaToRgba
exports.description: HSV → RGB with integer channels; hue 360 equals hue 0.
exports.signature: ({ h, s, v, a }: Hsva) => Rgba

exports.name: normalizeHex
exports.description: Any parseable colour string → canonical hex; null when it does not parse.

exports.name: parseColor
exports.description: Parses `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa` (leading `#` optional), `rgb()`/`rgba()` and `hsl()`/`hsla()`; null when malformed. Out-of-range channels clamp.

exports.name: readableOn
exports.description: Which of black or white reads better on `background`: for checkmarks on swatches and text on previews.

exports.name: relativeLuminance
exports.description: WCAG relative luminance 0–1; a translucent colour is first composited over white.

exports.name: rgbaToHsla
exports.description: RGB → HSL (via HSV).

exports.name: rgbaToHsva
exports.description: RGB → HSV. A grey (no saturation) reports hue 0; callers that care keep their own hue.
exports.signature: ({ r, g, b, a }: Rgba) => Hsva

exports.name: ColorFormat
exports.description: One of `COLOR_FORMATS`: a text format a color is shown or written in.

exports.name: Hsla
exports.description: Hue 0–360, saturation and lightness 0–100, alpha 0–1: the CSS `hsl()` model.

exports.name: Hsva
exports.description: Hue 0–360, saturation and value 0–100, alpha 0–1: the picker's working model.

exports.name: Rgba
exports.description: sRGB with alpha: channels 0–255, `a` 0–1.

exports.name: INLINE_EDIT_START_KEYS
exports.description: Keys on the shown value that start editing: Enter, and F2 as in spreadsheets.

exports.name: initialInlineEditState
exports.description: The idle state: nothing being edited.

exports.name: inlineEditKeyAction
exports.description:
The editor's key table: Escape cancels; Enter submits a single-line editor,
while a multi-line one keeps Enter for new lines and submits on Ctrl/⌘+Enter.
Shift+Enter in a single-line editor still submits (there is no new line to type).
exports.signature: (key: string, { multiline, mod }?: { readonly multiline?: boolean; readonly mod?: boolean; }) => InlineEditKeyAction | null

exports.name: inlineEditReducer
exports.description: The state after `event` (see file header). Events that make no sense in the current state return it unchanged.

exports.name: planSubmit
exports.description:
Plans a submit of `draft` against `before`: `busy` while one is pending,
`invalid` when `validate` returns a message, `unchanged` when the draft equals
the value from before editing (by `equals`, default `Object.is`), else `submit`.
exports.signature: <T>(state: InlineEditState<T>, draft: T, before: T, validate?: (draft: T) => string | null | undefined, equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean) => InlineEditSubmitPlan<T>

exports.name: submitErrorMessage
exports.description: The message shown for a rejected `onSubmit`: an Error's message, a string as is, else a generic line.

exports.name: InlineEditEvent
exports.description: What the inline-edit reducer reacts to: an edit starting, a draft change, a refusal, and the steps of a submit.

exports.name: InlineEditKeyAction
exports.description: What a key does in the editor.

exports.name: InlineEditSession
exports.description: One open edit: the value when editing began and the draft being typed.

props.name: session
props.description: The open edit, or null while the value is only shown.

props.name: error
props.description: The message from `validate` or a failed `onSubmit`; cleared by the next change.

props.name: pending
props.description: An async `onSubmit` is running; the editor is read-only meanwhile.

exports.name: InlineEditSubmitPlan
exports.description: What a submit should do, decided before any side effect.

exports.name: daysInMonth
exports.description: Days in `month` (1–12) of `year`, leap years included.

exports.name: parseIsoDate
exports.description: Parses `YYYY-MM-DD`; `null` for anything malformed or impossible (2026-02-30).

exports.name: toIsoDate
exports.description: Formats parts as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

exports.name: toUtcDate
exports.description: The UTC midnight `Date` of a plain date (for Intl formatting with `timeZone: "UTC"`).

exports.name: todayIso
exports.description: Today in the host's zone (the only place the host clock is read), or in `timeZone`.

exports.name: addDays
exports.description: `iso` plus `n` days (negative goes back).

exports.name: addMonths
exports.description: `iso` plus `n` months, with the day clamped to the target month (31 Jan + 1 month = 28/29 Feb).

exports.name: daysBetween
exports.description: Whole days from `a` to `b` (positive when `b` is later).

exports.name: endOfMonth
exports.description: The last day of the month holding `iso`.

exports.name: startOfWeek
exports.description: The first day of the week containing `iso`, for weeks starting on `weekStart`.

exports.name: clampIso
exports.description: Clamps `iso` into `[min, max]` (either bound optional).
exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, min?: IsoDate | null, max?: IsoDate | null) => IsoDate

exports.name: localeWeekStart
exports.description:
The locale's first day of the week. Uses `Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo` (or the
older `weekInfo` getter) where the engine has it, else Monday except for the
regions that start on Sunday or Saturday.

exports.name: localeWeekendDays
exports.description:
The locale's weekend days (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday): `Intl.Locale` week
info's `weekend` where the engine has it, else the CLDR regions above, else
Saturday and Sunday. A calendar tints these columns.

exports.name: localeMinimalDays
exports.description: The fewest days of a new year the locale's first week of the year must hold (week info's `minimalDays` where present).

exports.name: monthGrid
exports.description: The 6×7 grid for the month containing `iso`, starting on `weekStart`. Always 6 rows so the popover never jumps.

exports.name: weekdayLabels
exports.description:
Weekday headers in grid order: a compact label for the column and the long
name for screen readers. The compact label is the short name cut to two
letters when it is a short Latin-style abbreviation ("Mo", "Di"), else the
locale's narrow form, because cutting a word like Arabic "الأحد" leaves only
the article.
exports.signature: (locale: string | undefined, weekStart: Weekday) => { short: string; long: string; }[]

exports.name: monthNames
exports.description: Locale month names, January first.

exports.name: formatIsoDate
exports.description: Formats a plain date with Intl (`options` default to a medium date).
exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, locale?: string, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) => string

exports.name: formatMonthYear
exports.description: "October 2026" for a calendar caption.

exports.name: IsoDate
exports.description: An ISO calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

exports.name: PlainDate
exports.description: A calendar date split into its parts; `month` is 1–12.

exports.name: Weekday
exports.description: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, the `Date#getUTCDay` numbering.

exports.name: addYears
exports.description: `iso` plus `n` years, with 29 Feb clamped to 28 Feb in a common year.

exports.name: compareIso
exports.description: ISO strings sort lexically, so plain string comparison orders dates.

exports.name: weekdayOf
exports.description: The day of the week of `iso` (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday).

exports.name: startOfMonth
exports.description: The first day of the month holding `iso`.

exports.name: startOfYear
exports.description: 1 January of the year holding `iso`.

exports.name: endOfYear
exports.description: 31 December of the year holding `iso`.

exports.name: startOfQuarter
exports.description: The first day of the quarter holding `iso` (1 Jan, 1 Apr, 1 Jul or 1 Oct).

exports.name: DayCell
exports.description: One cell of a month grid.

exports.name: parseIsoTime
exports.description: Parses `HH:mm[:ss]`; `null` for anything malformed or out of range.

exports.name: toIsoTime
exports.description: Formats parts as `HH:mm`, or `HH:mm:ss` when `withSeconds`.

exports.name: localeUses12Hour
exports.description: True when the locale shows a 12-hour clock with a day period (en-US yes, de-DE no).

exports.name: formatIsoTime
exports.description: Formats a time with Intl: "2:30 PM" / "14:30".
exports.signature: (iso: IsoTime, locale?: string, opts?: { seconds?: boolean; hour12?: boolean; }) => string

exports.name: timeSlots
exports.description:
Times from `min` to `max` (inclusive) every `stepMinutes`, as `HH:mm`. The
list a time picker's popover offers; a bound that is not on the step grid is
rounded inward.
exports.signature: (stepMinutes: number, min?: IsoTime, max?: IsoTime) => IsoTime[]

exports.name: nearestSlot
exports.description: The slot nearest to `iso`, so the list opens scrolled to the current value.
exports.signature: (slots: readonly IsoTime[], iso: IsoTime | null) => IsoTime | null

exports.name: splitDateTime
exports.description: Splits `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm[:ss]` into its date and time; either may be null.
exports.signature: (value: IsoDateTime | null | undefined) => { date: IsoDate | null; time: IsoTime | null; }

exports.name: joinDateTime
exports.description: Joins a date and time; null unless both are present.
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate | null, time: IsoTime | null) => IsoDateTime | null

exports.name: formatIsoDateTime
exports.description: Formats a date-time with Intl: "15 Oct 2026, 14:30".

exports.name: secondsToTime
exports.description: Seconds since midnight → a wall time, wrapping past midnight either way.

exports.name: isoTimeSeconds
exports.description: Seconds since midnight of an ISO time, or null when it is not one.

exports.name: gridSeconds
exports.description: The seconds between two neighbouring times on the grid of `precision` and `steps` (an hour, `minuteStep` minutes or `secondStep` seconds).

exports.name: onTimeGrid
exports.description: True when `iso` sits on the grid: its minute a multiple of `minuteStep`, its second of `secondStep`, nothing finer than `precision`.
exports.signature: (iso: IsoTime, precision: TimeUnit, steps?: TimeSteps) => boolean

exports.name: snapTimeDown
exports.description: Rounds a time down onto the grid ("Now" at 14:37 with 15-minute steps is 14:30).
exports.signature: (iso: IsoTime, precision: TimeUnit, steps?: TimeSteps) => IsoTime | null

exports.name: timeGrid
exports.description:
Every time from `min` to `max` (inclusive) every `stepSeconds`, as ISO times
of `precision`: the list a time panel offers (a bound off the grid is
rounded inward). A floating wall time has every one of them on every day, a
DST day included (see `zonedDayTimes` for the times a zone actually has).
exports.signature: (stepSeconds: number, precision?: TimeUnit, min?: IsoTime, max?: IsoTime) => IsoTime[]

exports.name: timeColumnValues
exports.description: The values one column of a time panel offers: hours (0–23, or 12, 1–11 on a 12-hour clock), minutes or seconds on their step.
exports.signature: (unit: TimeUnit, hourCycle: HourCycle, steps?: TimeSteps) => number[]

exports.name: timeRangeSeconds
exports.description:
A time range's length in seconds. With `overnight`, an end before the start
runs past midnight (a 22:00–06:00 night shift is 8 hours); without it such a
range is negative, which the picker treats as backwards.
exports.signature: (start: IsoTime, end: IsoTime, overnight?: boolean) => number | null

exports.name: endOfDayTime
exports.description: The last time on the grid of the day (23:59, 23:59:59, or 23:45 with 15-minute steps).

exports.name: nowIsoTime
exports.description: The host clock's wall time as `HH:mm:ss` (in `timeZone` when given).

exports.name: formatTimeAt
exports.description:
Formats a time with Intl ("2:30 PM", "14:30", "2:30:15 PM" with seconds). An
hour-precision time keeps its minutes ("2:00 PM", "14:00"): a 24-hour "14"
alone does not read as a time. A 24-hour clock pads the hour ("09:00", as
the segments and the columns write it); a 12-hour one does not ("9:00 AM").
exports.signature: (iso: IsoTime, precision: TimeUnit, locale?: string, hourCycle?: HourCycle) => string

exports.name: IsoTime
exports.description: `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`, 24-hour.

exports.name: IsoDateTime
exports.description: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (or with `:ss`), a zone-free local date and time.

exports.name: PlainTime
exports.description: A wall-clock time as numbers (24-hour), the parsed form of an `IsoTime`.

exports.name: timeToMinutes
exports.description: Minutes since midnight, for comparing and stepping.

exports.name: minutesToTime
exports.description: The time `m` minutes after midnight, wrapped into one day (seconds 0).

exports.name: TIME_GRANULARITIES
exports.description:
How fine a picker's value is: `day` is a date alone; `hour`, `minute` and
`second` add a time of that precision. The value stays a floating ISO
date-time: an hour-precision value is
`2026-11-11T14:00`, a minute one `2026-11-11T14:30`, a second one
`2026-11-11T14:30:15`.

exports.name: TimeGranularity
exports.description: One of `TIME_GRANULARITIES`: the precision of a date-time value, from a bare day to seconds.

exports.name: TIME_UNITS
exports.description: The time units a panel edits, largest first; a precision is the smallest one shown.

exports.name: TimeUnit
exports.description: One of `TIME_UNITS`: a time unit a panel edits.

exports.name: HourCycle
exports.description: A 12- or 24-hour clock (`undefined` in an option means the locale's).

exports.name: SECONDS_PER_MINUTE
exports.description: Seconds in a minute.

exports.name: SECONDS_PER_HOUR
exports.description: Seconds in an hour.

exports.name: SECONDS_PER_DAY
exports.description: Seconds in a day.

exports.name: timeToSeconds
exports.description: Seconds since midnight (the seconds count, unlike `timeToMinutes`).

exports.name: compareIsoTime
exports.description: Compares two ISO times by their seconds (`14:30` equals `14:30:00`); a malformed one sorts first.

exports.name: granularityPrecision
exports.description: The time precision of a granularity; `day` has none.

exports.name: secondsToIsoTime
exports.description: Formats seconds since midnight as an ISO time of `precision` (`second` writes `:ss`).

exports.name: TimeSteps
exports.description: Steps per unit: hours always step by one; `minuteStep` and `secondStep` divide the hour and the minute.

exports.name: hourFrom12
exports.description: A 24-hour hour from a 12-hour clock's hour (12, 1–11) and day period (0 AM, 1 PM).

exports.name: dayPeriodOf
exports.description: The day period of a 24-hour hour: 0 before noon, 1 from noon.

exports.name: TimePresetContext
exports.description: What a time preset resolves against: the current wall time and the panel's grid.

exports.name: TimePreset
exports.description:
A named time (Now, Noon, End of day), as data like the range presets. The
built-in ids get their labels from the `pickers` catalog; a custom preset
brings its own `label`. `today` presets also set the date to today in a
date-time picker ("Now" means today, now).

exports.name: TIME_PRESET_IDS
exports.description: The built-in time presets' ids.

exports.name: DEFAULT_TIME_PRESETS
exports.description: Now (today), noon and the end of the day, each on the panel's grid.

exports.name: hourCycleOf
exports.description: A boolean `hour12` (the older props) as an hour cycle; undefined stays the locale's.

exports.name: localeHourCycle
exports.description: The hour cycle a locale shows when none is forced.

exports.name: rangeClick
exports.description:
The range after clicking `iso`. First click (or a click after a complete
range) starts a new one; the second click ends it, swapping when it lands
before the start, so the user can pick the two days in either order.

exports.name: previewRange
exports.description: The range to draw while the pointer hovers `hover` between the two clicks.

exports.name: inRange
exports.description: True when `iso` lies within a complete range (ends included).

exports.name: rangeLength
exports.description: Days in a complete range, ends included; 0 when incomplete.

exports.name: rangeCrossesDisabled
exports.description: True when any day of the range is disabled, so a range cannot span a blocked day.

exports.name: matchPreset
exports.description: The preset whose range equals `range` today, so the list can mark it; null when none does.
exports.signature: (range: DateRange, presets: readonly RangePreset[], ctx: PresetContext) => RangePreset | null

exports.name: formatDateRange
exports.description:
`Intl.DateTimeFormat#formatRange` with plain spaces: engines disagree on the spaces around the range dash (ICU 78 in
Node writes thin spaces, U+2009, where Chrome writes plain ones), so the same range would read differently on a server
and in a browser, and a server-rendered page would not hydrate. Thin and narrow no-break spaces become plain ones.
exports.signature: (format: Intl.DateTimeFormat, start: Date | number, end: Date | number) => string

exports.name: formatRange
exports.description: "15 – 21 Oct 2026" with Intl's range formatter (shares the common parts).
exports.signature: (range: DateRange, locale?: string, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) => string

exports.name: lengthBlocked
exports.description: Days the second click may not land on, given the first click and the length bounds.
exports.signature: (draft: DateRange, iso: IsoDate, minDays?: number, maxDays?: number) => boolean

exports.name: isRolling
exports.description: True when a value is a rolling range (any `{ start, end }` that names a preset).

exports.name: resolveRolling
exports.description: A rolling range's days today: its preset resolved against `ctx`, or its stored ends when no preset in the list has its id.
exports.signature: (value: RollingRange, presets: readonly RangePreset[], ctx: PresetContext) => DateRange

exports.name: rollingRange
exports.description: A preset picked today, as a rolling day range.

exports.name: previousPeriod
exports.description:
The range right before `range` with the same length ("compare to previous
period"). In days (the default; weeks are whole days too): Nov 1–30 → Oct
2–31, as analytics tools count it. In months, quarters or years the range
covers whole months and moves by as many: Sep–Nov → Jun–Aug, Q4 → Q3. Empty
for an incomplete or open-ended range.

exports.name: previousYear
exports.description:
The same range a year earlier ("compare to previous year"): the same dates
(29 Feb falls back to 28 Feb); whole months, quarters and years stay whole
(Feb 2024 → Feb 2023, ending on the 28th); a week range moves back 52 weeks so
it starts on the same weekday. Empty for an incomplete or open-ended range.

exports.name: compareRange
exports.description: The compare range of `range` for `kind`, counted in `unit` (see `previousPeriod` / `previousYear`).
exports.signature: (range: DateRange, kind: CompareKind, unit?: CompareUnit) => DateRange

exports.name: rangeLengthIn
exports.description: A complete range's length in `unit`: days counts both ends, nights one fewer; 0 when incomplete.

exports.name: inOpenRange
exports.description: True when `iso` lies within a range whose missing end is unbounded (a complete range as `inRange`).

exports.name: moveRangeEnd
exports.description:
The range with one end moved to `iso` (a drag of that end, or Shift+arrow
on it). Moving an end past the other swaps them, so the range stays in
order; the result says which end `iso` became, so a drag keeps holding it.
exports.signature: (range: DateRange, end: RangeEnd, iso: IsoDate) => { readonly range: DateRange; readonly end: RangeEnd; }

exports.name: DateRange
exports.description: An inclusive range; `end` is null while the user is between the two clicks.

exports.name: EMPTY_RANGE
exports.description: A range with neither end picked, the value of an empty range picker.

exports.name: PresetContext
exports.description: What a preset computes from: today and the locale's week start.

exports.name: RangePreset
exports.description: A named range a picker offers as a one-click shortcut.

exports.name: DEFAULT_RANGE_PRESETS
exports.description: The usual analytics presets. Pass your own list to the picker to change or translate them.

exports.name: DAY_PRESETS
exports.description: Single-day presets: today, yesterday, tomorrow, a week from today.

exports.name: WEEK_PRESETS
exports.description: Week presets (the locale's week): this, last and next week.

exports.name: WEEK_RANGE_PRESETS
exports.description: Week-range presets: the last 4 and 12 whole weeks up to this one.

exports.name: MONTH_PRESETS
exports.description: Month presets: this, last and next month.

exports.name: MONTH_RANGE_PRESETS
exports.description: Month-range presets: the last 3, 6 and 12 whole months up to this one, and the year so far.

exports.name: QUARTER_PRESETS
exports.description: Quarter presets: this, last and next quarter.

exports.name: QUARTER_RANGE_PRESETS
exports.description: Quarter-range presets: the last 4 quarters up to this one, and this year's quarters.

exports.name: YEAR_PRESETS
exports.description: Year presets: this, last and next year.

exports.name: YEAR_RANGE_PRESETS
exports.description: Year-range presets: the last 3 and 5 years up to this one.

exports.name: PresetMode
exports.description: The date modes a preset list is chosen for (`useDatePicker`'s modes but the time ones).

exports.name: PRESETS_BY_MODE
exports.description: The default preset list per mode: pass `presets={presetsForMode(mode)}`, or your own list, to a picker.

exports.name: presetsForMode
exports.description: The default presets for a mode.

exports.name: RollingRange
exports.description:
A range picked from a preset that stays relative to today: `{ preset:
"last-7", start, end }`. `start` / `end` are what it meant when it was
stored; a picker given it back re-resolves the preset against its own today
(`resolveRolling`), so "last 7 days" saved on Monday still means the last
seven days on Friday. An id the picker's presets do not know keeps the stored
ends. It is a `PeriodRange` with one more key, so code that reads `start` /
`end` keeps working.

exports.name: rollingPresetId
exports.description: The preset id a value names, if it is a rolling range.

exports.name: COMPARE_KINDS
exports.description: What a range is compared against: the same length right before it, or the same dates a year earlier.

exports.name: CompareKind
exports.description: One of `COMPARE_KINDS`: the previous period of the same length, or the same dates a year earlier.

exports.name: CompareUnit
exports.description: The unit a range counts in for `previousPeriod`: days, or whole weeks, months, quarters or years.

exports.name: LENGTH_UNITS
exports.description: What a range's length counts: days (both ends, a weekend is 2) or nights (a stay from Fri to Sun is 2).

exports.name: LengthUnit
exports.description: One of `LENGTH_UNITS`: whether a range's length counts days or nights.

exports.name: lengthInDays
exports.description: A length bound in `unit` as the inclusive day count `lengthBlocked` reads (n nights span n + 1 days).
exports.signature: (length: number | undefined, unit: LengthUnit) => number | undefined

exports.name: isOpenRange
exports.description: True when a range has exactly one end ("from 1 Jan", "until 31 Mar"): an `openEnded` picker's value.

exports.name: RangeEnd
exports.description: Which end of a range.

exports.name: toIsoQuarter
exports.description: The quarter `iso` falls in, `YYYY-Qn`.

exports.name: parseIsoMonth
exports.description: `YYYY-MM` → year and month (1–12); null when malformed.
exports.signature: (value: string | null | undefined) => { readonly year: number; readonly month: number; } | null

exports.name: parseIsoQuarter
exports.description: `YYYY-Qn` → year and quarter (1–4); null when malformed.
exports.signature: (value: string | null | undefined) => { readonly year: number; readonly quarter: number; } | null

exports.name: parseIsoYear
exports.description: `YYYY` → the year; null when malformed.

exports.name: isoWeekId
exports.description: The ISO 8601 week `iso` falls in, e.g. `2026-W46` (Thursday rule: 2027-01-01 is `2026-W53`).

exports.name: isoWeekStart
exports.description: The Monday an ISO week id starts on; null when malformed or past the year's last week.

exports.name: localeWeekIsoId
exports.description: The ISO week id of a locale week starting on `weekStart` (see {@link MAJORITY_DAY_OFFSET}).

exports.name: weekNumberOf
exports.description:
The week number of the week row starting on `weekStartDay`.
`iso`: the ISO week sharing most of the row's days ({@link localeWeekIsoId}),
the number `details.isoWeek` carries. `locale`: the locale's week-of-year:
week 1 is the first row holding at least `minimalDays` days of the new year
(1 in the US: the row with 1 January; 4 in most of Europe, which with a
Monday start is the ISO rule).
exports.signature: (weekStartDay: IsoDate, numbering: WeekNumbering, minimalDays?: number) => number

exports.name: periodStart
exports.description: The first day of the period of `unit` containing `iso`.
exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, unit: PeriodUnit, weekStart?: Weekday) => IsoDate

exports.name: periodEnd
exports.description: The last day of the period of `unit` containing `iso`.

exports.name: periodRangeOf

exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, unit: PeriodUnit, weekStart?: Weekday) => DateRange

exports.name: addPeriods

exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, unit: PeriodUnit, n: number) => IsoDate

exports.name: periodKey
exports.description: The value string of the month, quarter or year containing `iso`.

exports.name: periodKeyRange
exports.description: The day bounds of a month, quarter or year value; null when the string is not one.

exports.name: periodRangeClick
exports.description:
The range after clicking the period of `unit` around `iso`: the first click
(or a click after a complete range) starts at that period, the second ends at
the other one's last day, in either order. For `day` this is `rangeClick`.

exports.name: previewPeriodRange
exports.description: The range to draw while hovering `hover` between the two clicks, snapped to whole periods.

exports.name: periodCount

exports.signature: (range: DateRange, unit: PeriodUnit, weekStart?: Weekday) => number

exports.name: formatPeriodKey

exports.signature: (key: string, unit: KeyedPeriodUnit, locale?: string, quarterLabel?: string) => string

exports.name: formatPeriodRange
exports.description:
A day range of whole periods for display: days and weeks through Intl's range
formatter (`16 – 22 Nov 2026`), months, quarters and years by their names
(`January 2026 – March 2026`, `Q1 2026 – Q2 2026`); a single period shows once.

exports.name: IsoMonth

exports.name: IsoQuarter
