exports.name: IsoYear
exports.description: A calendar year, `YYYY`.

exports.name: IsoWeekId
exports.description: An ISO 8601 week id, `YYYY-Www` (Monday-based, week-numbering year by the Thursday rule).

exports.name: PeriodUnit
exports.description: What one cell of a calendar stands for.

exports.name: KeyedPeriodUnit
exports.description: The units with a string value of their own (a week's value is a day range).

exports.name: PeriodRange
exports.description: An inclusive range of periods of one kind; `end` is null between the two clicks.

exports.name: toIsoMonth
exports.description: The month `iso` falls in, `YYYY-MM`.

exports.name: toIsoYear
exports.description: The year `iso` falls in, `YYYY`.

exports.name: WEEK_NUMBERINGS
exports.description: How a calendar numbers its week rows: ISO 8601 weeks, or the locale's own week-of-year.

exports.name: WeekNumbering
exports.description: One of `WEEK_NUMBERINGS`: ISO weeks or the locale's own week-of-year.

exports.name: QUARTER_LABEL
exports.description: Default English quarter label; the picker passes the `pickers` catalog's instead.

exports.name: resolveCalendarId
exports.description:
The calendar a picker draws: the `calendar` option, else the locale's
`-u-ca-` extension, else Gregorian. An id this module does not draw (or the
engine cannot format) falls back to Gregorian.

exports.name: calendarLocale
exports.description:
`locale` with `calendar` pinned as its `-u-ca-` extension, so every Intl label
made with it is in that calendar. Returned unchanged (even `undefined`) when
the locale already formats in that calendar, so the usual en-US + Gregorian
case formats exactly as before.
exports.signature: (locale: string | undefined, calendar: CalendarId) => string | undefined

exports.name: calendarFields
exports.description: The engine's fields for `iso` in `calendar` (read from `formatToParts`, Latin digits, English month identities).

exports.name: calendarSystem
exports.description: The system for a calendar id (cached; the Gregorian one is the date core itself).

exports.name: calendarMonthGrid
exports.description:
The 6×7 grid of the calendar month containing `iso`, starting on
`weekStart`: every cell's `day` is its day in that calendar, and `inMonth`
marks the calendar month's own days. The Gregorian grid is `monthGrid` itself.
exports.signature: (system: CalendarSystem, iso: IsoDate, weekStart: Weekday) => DayCell[][]

exports.name: calendarMonthsFrom
exports.description: `count` consecutive calendar months from the one containing `first` (their first days).
exports.signature: (system: CalendarSystem, first: IsoDate, count: number) => IsoDate[]

exports.name: calendarMonthsBetween
exports.description: How many calendar months from the one containing `a` to the one containing `b` (0 for the same month, negative when `b` is earlier).
exports.signature: (system: CalendarSystem, a: IsoDate, b: IsoDate) => number

exports.name: calendarYearPage
exports.description: The year page of the years view: `size` calendar years from a multiple of `size`, as their first days.
exports.signature: (system: CalendarSystem, iso: IsoDate, size: number) => IsoDate[]

exports.name: gregorianMonthsCovering
exports.description: Gregorian months the given calendar months touch (any day in each), for loaders keyed by Gregorian month.

exports.name: formatCalendarMonth
exports.description: A month's name in `locale` (already pinned to the calendar with `calendarLocale`).
exports.signature: (iso: IsoDate, locale: string | undefined, width?: "long" | "short") => string

exports.name: formatCalendarYear
exports.description: A year's name in `locale` (pinned to the calendar): `1405`, `2569 BE`, `Reiwa 1` / `令和元年`.

exports.name: CALENDAR_IDS
exports.description: The calendar systems a calendar can be drawn in (the Intl ids).

exports.name: CalendarId
exports.description: One of `CALENDAR_IDS`: an Intl calendar system a calendar can be drawn in.

exports.name: isCalendarId
exports.description: Whether `value` is one of the supported `CALENDAR_IDS`.
exports.signature: (value: string | null | undefined) => value is CalendarId

exports.name: CalendarFields
exports.description: One day's fields in a calendar: the era, the year in it, the month's name (its identity) and the day of the month.

exports.name: CalendarSystem
exports.description:
A calendar's months and years over ISO days: everything the calendar hook
pages, drills and draws by. Every method takes and returns ISO Gregorian
dates; a "month" is named by its first day.

exports.name: GREGORIAN
exports.description: The Gregorian system, the default everywhere a calendar is not given.

exports.name: fieldLayout
exports.description:
The locale's field layout, read from `Intl.DateTimeFormat#formatToParts` on a
sample date so order and separators match how the locale writes dates.

exports.name: segmentBounds
exports.description: Inclusive bounds of a segment given the others (the day's max depends on month and year).
exports.signature: (kind: SegmentKind, values: SegmentValues, hour12: boolean) => { min: number; max: number; }

exports.name: typeDigit
exports.description:
Types one digit into a segment. Digits accumulate in `buffer`; focus moves
on as soon as no further digit could keep the value in bounds (typing "4"
into a month is April and moves on, "1" waits for a possible "0"–"2"). A
digit that would overflow starts over from that digit.
exports.signature: (kind: SegmentKind, buffer: string, digit: string, bounds: { min: number; max: number; }) => TypeResult

exports.name: stepSegment
exports.description: Steps a segment by `delta`, wrapping within its bounds; an empty segment starts from `fallback`.
exports.signature: (value: number | undefined, delta: number, bounds: { min: number; max: number; }, fallback: number) => number

exports.name: segmentPlaceholder
exports.description: The placeholder shown in an empty segment.

exports.name: segmentText
exports.description: The text a filled segment shows: zero-padded numbers, the locale's AM/PM.
exports.signature: (kind: SegmentKind, value: number, locale?: string) => string

exports.name: dayPeriodLabels
exports.description: The locale's AM and PM labels.

exports.name: valuesFrom
exports.description: Splits a date and/or time value into segment values (a period field reads its period from the first day).
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate | null, time: IsoTime | null, hour12: boolean, field?: FieldUnit) => SegmentValues

exports.name: valuesTo
exports.description: Segment values → `{ date, time }` once every required segment holds a valid value; nulls otherwise.
exports.signature: (layout: readonly LayoutPart[], values: SegmentValues, weekStart?: Weekday) => { date: IsoDate | null; time: IsoTime | null; complete: boolean; }

exports.name: SEGMENT_KINDS
exports.description: The parts a segmented date or time field can show, largest first, with the AM/PM `dayPeriod` last.

exports.name: SegmentKind
exports.description: One of `SEGMENT_KINDS`: a part of a segmented date or time field.

exports.name: LayoutPart
exports.description: One slot of a field's layout: an editable segment or the literal text between two.

exports.name: TimePrecision
exports.description: The smallest time unit a field edits (`second` is the same as `seconds: true`).

exports.name: FieldShape
exports.description: What a field edits.

exports.name: SegmentValues
exports.description: Segment values while editing; a missing key is an empty segment. `dayPeriod` is 0 (AM) or 1 (PM).

exports.name: layoutIs12Hour
exports.description: True when the layout has a day-period segment (a 12-hour clock).

exports.name: TypeResult
exports.description: The result of typing into a segment: the new value, the pending digits, and whether focus moves on.

exports.name: FieldUnit
exports.description: Where a date field's value sits: a day, or the first day of a week, month, quarter or year.

exports.name: numericDateOrder
exports.description: The locale's numeric date order, read from Intl (en-US MDY, en-GB and de-DE DMY, ja YMD).

exports.name: parsePhrase
exports.description: Reads `text` into what it means (see the file header); `invalid` or `incomplete` when it cannot.

exports.name: fitPhrase
exports.description:
Fits a phrase to what a picker holds: a day where a week, month, quarter or
year is wanted stands for the one containing it; a period of the picker's unit
or a coarser one fills a range of that unit; a single day in a range picker is
`incomplete`; anything else is `wrong-kind` (a range in a single-day picker).
exports.signature: (phrase: ParsedPhrase, target: ParseTarget, weekStart: Weekday) => FitResult

exports.name: selectionStart
exports.description: The first day a selection names: the day, the first listed day, or a range's start.

exports.name: selectionError
exports.description:
The rule a value breaks, if any: `out-of-range` when a day (or a range end)
falls outside `min`/`max` (a period only when it lies wholly outside), then
`disabled` when a picked day is blocked, or (week, month, quarter and year
values) when every day of the first or last period is: the rule the drill
views draw a period cell disabled by.
exports.signature: (value: Selection | null, unit: PeriodUnit, rules: SelectionRules) => DateRuleError | undefined

exports.name: parseSelection
exports.description: Parses `text` for a picker: the phrase, fitted to the target, checked against the rules.
exports.signature: (text: string, target: ParseTarget, ctx: ParseContext & SelectionRules) => ParseOutcome

exports.name: formatSelectionText
exports.description:
A value as text the parser reads back to the same value (the text field shows
it): a medium date, days joined by `; `, a range's ends formatted one by one,
a week as `2026-W46`, a month by name, a quarter as `Q4 2026`, a year.
exports.signature: (value: Selection | null, target: ParseTarget, ctx: FormatTextContext) => string

exports.name: formatDateTimeText
exports.description:
A date and a time as text the parser reads back to the same pair (a date-time picker's text field shows it): the
medium date, a space, then the locale's time ("Nov 15, 2026 3:30 PM", "15.11.2026 15:30", "2026. 11. 15. 오후 3:30").
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate, time: IsoTime, ctx?: FormatDateTimeContext) => string

exports.name: acceptedFormats
exports.description: Today in the formats a picker of `target` accepts, the locale's first (the field's hint).
exports.signature: (target: ParseTarget, ctx: FormatTextContext & { readonly today: IsoDate; }) => readonly AcceptedFormat[]

exports.name: isoWeeksInYear
exports.description: Weeks in an ISO week-numbering year (52 or 53): the week of 28 December is always the last.

exports.name: shiftSelection
exports.description: Shifts a selection by `n` periods of `unit` (the field's + and − keys): a day, each listed day, or both range ends.
exports.signature: (value: Selection, unit: PeriodUnit, n: number, weekStart: Weekday) => Selection

exports.name: todaySelection
exports.description: The whole period of `unit` around today as a selection of `target`'s shape (the T key).
exports.signature: (target: ParseTarget, today: IsoDate, weekStart: Weekday) => Selection

exports.name: fitRangeToTarget
exports.description:
A day range (what a preset resolves to) fitted to what a picker holds: a
single day takes its start; a week, month, quarter or year the period holding
its start; a range of days stays; a range of periods covers the whole periods
from its start to its end; a list of days lists every day in it (at most a
year's worth). Open-ended ranges keep their missing end (range targets only).
exports.signature: (range: DateRange, target: ParseTarget, weekStart: Weekday) => Selection | null

exports.name: PARSE_WORDS
exports.description:
The grammar's English words, by `pickers` catalog key. Each value lists the
accepted words separated by `|`; the weekday and month keys list seven and
twelve groups separated by `|`, each group's spellings separated by spaces
(Sunday first, January first). Translate them in a locale bundle like any key.

exports.name: ParseWords
exports.description: The grammar's vocabulary: every `PARSE_WORDS` key as a (translated) string.

exports.name: DATE_FIELD_ERRORS
exports.description: Why a typed or parsed value was refused, or committed but breaks a rule. Each has a `pickers` catalog message.

exports.name: DateFieldError
exports.description: One of `DATE_FIELD_ERRORS`: why a typed or parsed value was refused or breaks a rule.

exports.name: DateRuleError
exports.description:
The errors that still leave a value to commit (it is stored and marked
invalid, like a typed segment value). `skipped-time` / `repeated-time` come
from a zoned picker with `disambiguation="reject"`: the
typed wall time stays in the field, the value is null (no instant), and the
code is `details.error`.

exports.name: NumericOrder
exports.description: The order of a numeric date's parts.

exports.name: ParsedPhrase
exports.description: What a text means before it meets a picker (see the file header).

exports.name: PhraseResult
exports.description: The outcome of parsing a phrase: the parsed phrase, or why it could not be read (`invalid` or `incomplete`).

exports.name: ParseContext
exports.description: What the parser reads against.

exports.name: SelectionKind
exports.description: How many values a picker holds.

exports.name: ParseTarget
exports.description: What a picker holds: one, many or a range of days or of whole periods.

exports.name: Selection
exports.description:
A picker value in the calendar's terms: a day, a list of days, or a day range
(a week, month, quarter or year, and their ranges, are day ranges covering
whole periods), the shapes `useCalendar` holds.

exports.name: SelectionRules
exports.description: The rules a fitted value is checked against.

exports.name: ParseOutcome
exports.description: A parse that a picker may commit (maybe with a rule error), or why it may not.

exports.name: FormatTextContext
exports.description: What formatting a value as text needs.

exports.name: RANGE_TEXT_JOIN
exports.description: Joins a range's two ends in text; the parser splits on it.

exports.name: LIST_TEXT_JOIN
exports.description: Joins a list of days in text (`;`, as a medium date can hold a comma).

exports.name: FormatDateTimeContext
exports.description: How a date-time is written as text: the locale, seconds or not, and the clock (`hour12`; default the locale's).

exports.name: AcceptedFormat
exports.description: One accepted way to write a value, for the field's hint.

exports.name: hasDateRules
exports.description: True when a set can block any day at all (a calendar with none skips its reason line and its period scans).

exports.name: compileDateRules
exports.description:
The one evaluator (see the file header): compiles a set once and answers per
day with the first block that matches. Compile it once per render, not per
day: the rules' indexes are built here.

exports.name: dateBlock
exports.description: One day's first block under a set (compiles the set: for many days, compile once with `compileDateRules`).

exports.name: isDisabledResult
exports.description: A host's `isDateDisabled` as the boolean the older APIs take (a `{ reason }` answer blocks).

exports.name: periodBlocked
exports.description:
A whole period's block: the block of its first day when EVERY day from
`start` to `end` is blocked (a month cell in the drill view, a year), else
null. A period wholly outside the bounds answers at once; otherwise the days
are scanned and the scan stops at the first open day.
exports.signature: (start: IsoDate, end: IsoDate, check: DateRuleCheck, set?: DateRuleSet) => DateBlock | null

exports.name: dateRuleSetFromJson
exports.description:
A rule set read from untrusted JSON (a form definition's `dateRules` args on
a server): the data fields only (`min`, `max`, `disablePast`,
`disableFuture`, `today`, `rules`); malformed entries are dropped.

exports.name: DATE_BLOCK_CODES
exports.description: Why a day is blocked: outside `min` / `max`, in the past or future, by a rule, by `isDateDisabled`, or by the day data.

exports.name: DateBlockCode
exports.description: One of `DATE_BLOCK_CODES`: why a day is blocked.

exports.name: DateBlock
exports.description: One verdict: why the day is blocked and, when the rule said so, the reason to show.

exports.name: DateRuleDay
exports.description: One listed day of a `dates` rule: the day alone, or with its own reason (a named holiday).

exports.name: DateRuleSpan
exports.description: One span of a `ranges` rule, both ends included, optionally with its own reason.

exports.name: WeekdaysRule
exports.description: Days of the week (0 Sunday … 6 Saturday) that may not be picked.

exports.name: DatesRule
exports.description: Listed days; a day's own reason wins over the rule's.

exports.name: RangesRule
exports.description: Listed spans; a span's own reason wins over the rule's.

exports.name: BeforeRule
exports.description: Every day strictly before `before`.

exports.name: AfterRule
exports.description: Every day strictly after `after`.

exports.name: DateRule
exports.description: One rule as data (see the file header).

exports.name: DateDisabledResult
exports.description: What a host's `isDateDisabled` may answer: a plain yes / no, or a block with the reason to show.

exports.name: DateDisabledFn
exports.description: A host's own day check (`isDateDisabled`); a boolean-only one keeps working unchanged.

exports.name: DayVerdict
exports.description: The verdict part of one day's async data (`DayDatum` adds the label and tone).

exports.name: DAY_TONES
exports.description: How a day's label is coloured: the default text, or a meaning (a cheap fare is `positive`, a dear one `negative`).

exports.name: DayTone
exports.description: One of `DAY_TONES`: how a day's label is coloured.

exports.name: DayDatum
exports.description: One day's async data (`dayData`): a label under the number (a price), its tone, and a verdict with its reason.

exports.name: DayDataRange
exports.description: The days one `dayData` call covers: one visible month, first day to last.

exports.name: DayDataLoader
exports.description:
The async day data loader: called once per visible month that is not cached
yet, with that month's days and an abort signal (aborted when the data key
changes or the calendar goes away); resolves to the data of the days it
knows (a day it leaves out has none).

exports.name: DateRuleSet
exports.description: Everything that can block a day (see the file header for the order they are read in).

exports.name: DateRuleCheck
exports.description: The compiled evaluator: a day's first block, or null when it may be picked.

exports.name: DateRuleSetJson
exports.description: A rule set as JSON: what a form definition carries in its `dateRules` args.

exports.name: DateRuleJson
exports.description: One rule as JSON (the `DateRule` shapes, written out so the table needs no types beyond JSON).

exports.name: DateRuleCase
exports.description: One case: under `set`, day `iso` answers `expect`.

exports.name: CONFORMANCE_TODAY
exports.description: The fixed "today" of every case that reads it (a Friday).

exports.name: DATE_RULE_CONFORMANCE
exports.description: The table (see the file header).

exports.name: hm
exports.description: Parse "09:30" into minutes from midnight.

exports.name: weeklyHours
exports.description: Weekly hours from a compact map: `{ 1: [["09:00", "17:00"]], ... }`.
exports.signature: (byDay: { readonly [weekday: number]: readonly (readonly [string, string])[]; }) => readonly (readonly TimeRange[])[]

exports.name: windowsOn
exports.description: The host's open windows on one host-local date, as instants (a window across a DST change is as long as the clocks make it).

exports.name: slotsForDay
exports.description:
Bookable slots on `viewerDate` in `viewerTimeZone` (see the file header for
the rules). Walks the host-local dates that can touch the invitee's day (a
day either side covers every offset), steps through each open window, and
keeps the starts that pass every rule, sorted.

exports.name: availableDates
exports.description: Which dates of a list have at least one slot (for greying calendar days).
exports.signature: (input: Omit<SlotsForDayInput, "viewerDate"> & { readonly dates: readonly IsoDate[]; }) => ReadonlySet<IsoDate>

exports.name: minutesInZone
exports.description: The minutes of the day an instant reads in a zone.

exports.name: dayPartOf
exports.description: The day part an instant falls in, on the invitee's clock.

exports.name: groupSlotsByDayPart
exports.description: Slots split into morning / afternoon / evening by the invitee's clock, empty parts left out, order kept.
exports.signature: <S extends Interval>(slots: readonly S[], timeZone: string) => readonly { readonly part: SlotDayPart; readonly slots: readonly S[]; }[]

exports.name: slotValueOf
exports.description: A slot as the picker's value (two `Z` instants).

exports.name: slotFromValue
exports.description: A value back to a slot (any instant string `parseToEpoch` reads); null when either end is unreadable or the end is not after the start.

exports.name: slotPageOf
exports.description: The first day of the page holding `date`: the 1st of its month, or its week's first day.
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate, unit: SlotPageUnit, weekStart: Weekday) => IsoDate

exports.name: addSlotPages
exports.description: The page `delta` pages from `page` (negative goes back).
exports.signature: (page: IsoDate, unit: SlotPageUnit, delta: number) => IsoDate

exports.name: slotPageDays
exports.description: The days of a page, first to last.

exports.name: slotPageRange
exports.description: The instants a page covers in a zone: its first day's midnight to the next page's.
exports.signature: (page: IsoDate, unit: SlotPageUnit, timeZone: string) => Interval

exports.name: firstSlotPageStep
exports.description:
One step of the page search, pure so it can be tested with a fixed clock:
stay on a page with a slot (`done`), or page forward one, or, once the next
page would pass the horizon (`horizonDays` from `now`, read in `timeZone`)
or the cap ({@link MAX_AUTO_PAGES} from today's page), go back `home` and
stop (`found: false`).
exports.signature: (input: SlotPageStepInput) => { readonly page: IsoDate; readonly done: boolean; readonly found: boolean; }

exports.name: slotTimeFormatOptions
exports.description: Intl options of a slot's time: hour and minute on the invitee's clock, 12 or 24 hours.

exports.name: formatSlotTime
exports.description: "9:00 AM" or "09:00": an instant on the invitee's clock (the formatter is cached per locale, zone and cycle).
exports.signature: (epoch: number, timeZone: string, locale?: string, hourCycle?: HourCycle) => string

exports.name: moveSlotFocus
exports.description:
The arrow-key maths of a slot grid: columns of different lengths (one per
day in the week layout; one column in the month layout's list). Up / Down
move within a column and stop at its ends; Left / Right go to the nearest
non-empty column that way, at the same row or its last; Home / End go to the
column's first and last slot. Null when the key goes nowhere.
exports.signature: (lengths: readonly number[], at: SlotGridPosition, key: SlotGridKey, rtl?: boolean) => SlotGridPosition | null

exports.name: TimeRange
exports.description: Minutes from local midnight, start inclusive, end exclusive: 540–1020 is 09:00–17:00.

exports.name: Availability
exports.description: The host's published hours.

exports.name: Interval
exports.description: An interval in epoch ms, end exclusive.

exports.name: Slot
exports.description: One bookable slot. `id` is the start as a string, stable across reloads.

props.name: id
props.description: The slot's start in epoch ms as a string; stable across reloads, so it can key a list or a selection.

props.name: remaining
props.description: Seats still free (1 for a one-to-one meeting).

props.name: start
props.description: Start of the interval, in epoch ms (included).

props.name: end
props.description: End of the interval, in epoch ms (excluded).

exports.name: SlotValue
exports.description: A slot as the picker's value: two UTC instants (`2026-11-11T14:00:00Z`).

exports.name: SlotRules
exports.description: How bookable slots are cut from availability: the meeting length, the step between starts, buffers and notice.

exports.name: SlotData
exports.description: What an availability adapter answers for a range of instants: the hours, the busy blocks, and this event's own bookings.

exports.name: SlotAvailabilityAdapter
exports.description:
Where a slot picker's availability comes from (the commerce kit's
`BookingAdapter` shape): called with the instants a page shows (a month or
a week in the invitee's zone), once per page.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DURATIONS
exports.description: The meeting lengths most booking pages offer.

exports.name: DEFAULT_STEP_CAP
exports.description: The longest default step between starts: a two-hour meeting still starts on every half hour.

exports.name: MINUTE_MS
exports.description: One minute and one day in ms.

exports.name: DAY_MS
exports.description: One day in ms.

exports.name: SlotsForDayInput
exports.description: Everything `slotsForDay` reads.

exports.name: SLOT_DAY_PARTS
exports.description: The parts of a day slots are grouped by, each up to (not including) `until` minutes of the invitee's clock. Labels are in the pickers catalog.

exports.name: SlotDayPart
exports.description: One of the `SLOT_DAY_PARTS` ids: the part of the day (`morning`, `afternoon`, `evening`) a slot is grouped under.

exports.name: SLOT_PAGE_UNITS
exports.description: The pages a slot picker shows: a month or a week.

exports.name: SlotPageUnit
exports.description: One of `SLOT_PAGE_UNITS`: whether a slot picker pages by month or by week.

exports.name: MAX_AUTO_MONTHS
exports.description:
How far the page search goes on its own looking for a page with a slot,
when the host names no month (the opening page) or the invitee asks for the
next available time: a year of months, or a quarter of weeks. Past it the
search gives up (see {@link firstSlotPageStep}).

exports.name: MAX_AUTO_WEEKS
exports.description: How many weeks the page search looks ahead on its own (a quarter); see `MAX_AUTO_MONTHS`.

exports.name: MAX_AUTO_PAGES
exports.description: The page search's limit per page unit: `MAX_AUTO_MONTHS` months or `MAX_AUTO_WEEKS` weeks.

exports.name: SlotPageStepInput
exports.description: One step of the page search's input.

exports.name: SLOT_GRID_KEYS
exports.description: The keys a slot grid answers (Left / Right are mirrored under RTL by the caller's `rtl`).

exports.name: SlotGridKey
exports.description: One of `SLOT_GRID_KEYS`: a key a slot grid moves the focus with.

exports.name: SlotGridPosition
exports.description: A position in a slot grid: a day column and a row in it.

exports.name: weekOfMonth
exports.description: Which week of its month `iso` falls in (1–5), and whether it is that weekday's last one.

exports.name: defaultRule
exports.description: The editor's starting rule for an event on `start`: weekly on its weekday, monthly on its date, ending never.

exports.name: monthlyChoices
exports.description: The monthly options a start date offers; "last" appears only when the start is in its weekday's last week.

exports.name: buildRRule
exports.description:
The canonical RRULE value (no `RRULE:` prefix): FREQ, INTERVAL (omitted when
1), BYDAY / BYMONTHDAY for the active mode, then COUNT or UNTIL (`YYYYMMDD`).

exports.name: parseRRuleParts
exports.description:
Reads an RRULE value (with or without the `RRULE:` prefix, any case). `undefined` when FREQ is missing or not one of
the four frequencies. Lenient like a calendar must be with what other software wrote: a value that does not read is
skipped (and named in `invalid`), a part it does not know is kept in `unsupported`, a repeated part's last value wins.

exports.name: formatRRuleParts
exports.description: Writes the parts back as `FREQ=…;…` (no prefix): INTERVAL when over 1, the BY parts, COUNT, UNTIL, then WKST when not Monday.

exports.name: expandRRuleParts
exports.description:
The dates the rule produces from `start` (the first occurrence when it matches, as RFC 5545 counts it), in order,
honouring COUNT and UNTIL; stop iterating whenever you have enough. Dates before `start` in its own period are
skipped, and so are days a month lacks (BYMONTHDAY=31 has no April; 29 February in a yearly rule's common years):
RFC 5545 semantics, not clamping. At most `MAX_RRULE_PERIODS` periods are walked.
exports.signature: (parts: RRuleParts, start: IsoDate, options?: ExpandRRuleOptions) => Generator<IsoDate, void, undefined>

exports.name: describeRRuleParts
exports.description: A short English summary of any rule the grammar reads: "Every 2 weeks on Mon, Wed · 10 times" (day and month names follow `locale`).

exports.name: parseRRule
exports.description:
Parses an RRULE value (with or without the `RRULE:` prefix) into editor
state; fields the value does not set come from `fallback` (pass
`defaultRule(start)` so a bare `FREQ=MONTHLY` picks the start's day). `null`
for anything malformed or outside the model. Reads the value with
`parseRRuleParts`, then keeps only what the editor can show exactly.

exports.name: ruleParts
exports.description: The editor's rule as grammar parts (what `buildRRule` writes, read back).

exports.name: occurrences
exports.description:
The first `limit` dates the rule produces on or after `start`, honouring
COUNT and UNTIL (`expandRRuleParts` over the rule's parts).
exports.signature: (rule: RecurrenceRule, start: IsoDate, limit: number) => IsoDate[]

exports.name: weekdayLongName
exports.description: A weekday's long name in `locale` (2023-01-01 was a Sunday).

exports.name: summarizeRule
exports.description:
A one-line description: "Every 2 weeks on Monday and Wednesday, 10 times",
"Monthly on the last Friday until Dec 31, 2026". Day and month names, the
weekday list, the until date and plural choice follow `locale` through Intl;
the sentence frame comes from `phrases` (English by default).
exports.signature: (rule: RecurrenceRule, start: IsoDate, locale?: string, phrases?: RecurrencePhrases) => string

exports.name: RECURRENCE_FREQUENCIES
exports.description: The frequencies the editor offers (RFC 5545 FREQ values).

exports.name: RecurrenceFrequency
exports.description: One of `RECURRENCE_FREQUENCIES`: how often a rule repeats (an RFC 5545 FREQ value).

exports.name: RECURRENCE_ENDS
exports.description: How a rule ends: `never`, after `count` occurrences, or on the `until` date (inclusive).

exports.name: RecurrenceEnd
exports.description: One of `RECURRENCE_ENDS`: how a rule ends.

exports.name: WEEK_ORDINALS
exports.description: Which week of the month a monthly-by-weekday rule picks; -1 is "the last".

exports.name: WeekOrdinal
exports.description: One of `WEEK_ORDINALS`: the week of the month a monthly-by-weekday rule picks; -1 is the last.

exports.name: WEEKDAY_CODES
exports.description: RRULE weekday codes indexed by `Weekday` (0 = Sunday, the `getUTCDay` numbering).

exports.name: WeekdayCode
exports.description: One of `WEEKDAY_CODES`: an RRULE weekday code (`SU` … `SA`).

exports.name: RecurrenceRule
exports.description:
The editor's state. Flat on purpose: switching WEEKLY → MONTHLY → WEEKLY keeps
the chosen weekdays, because every field survives whichever `freq` is active.
`buildRRule` writes only the fields the active `freq` / `monthlyMode` / `end` use.

exports.name: DEFAULT_RECURRENCE_COUNT
exports.description: Default occurrence count when the user switches the end to "after N".

exports.name: MAX_RRULE_PERIODS
exports.description: A safety cap on the periods an expansion walks, so a rule that never matches (BYMONTHDAY=31 every 12 months from February) terminates.

exports.name: weekdayFromIndex
exports.description: Any integer folded onto a `Weekday` (7 → 0, -1 → 6), for "week start + i" loops.

exports.name: MonthlyChoice
exports.description: One monthly choice derived from the start date ("on day 15", "on the third Tuesday", "on the last Friday").

exports.name: RRuleByDay
exports.description: One BYDAY entry: a weekday, with an ordinal for MONTHLY / YEARLY rules.

exports.name: RRuleUntil
exports.description: UNTIL as written: a DATE, or a DATE-TIME in wall time or (with `utc`) an instant.

exports.name: RRuleParts
exports.description: Every part of an RRULE the grammar reads.

exports.name: ExpandRRuleOptions
exports.description: Options for `expandRRuleParts`.

exports.name: RecurrencePhrases
exports.description: The words of a summary; swap them for another language (day and month names, lists and dates already follow `locale`).

exports.name: ENGLISH_RECURRENCE_PHRASES
exports.description: English summary phrases (the default).

exports.name: canonicalZone
exports.description: The current IANA id for `zone` (`Asia/Calcutta` → `Asia/Kolkata`), kept as-is when the engine does not accept the new id.

exports.name: listTimeZones
exports.description: Every IANA zone the engine knows under its current id, sorted, plus `UTC`.

exports.name: detectTimeZone
exports.description: The host's zone under its current id, `UTC` when the engine cannot tell.

exports.name: isValidTimeZone
exports.description: True when `zone` is a fixed offset (`UTC+05:30`, `+05:30`; zone.ts does their maths without Intl) or an id the engine accepts as a `timeZone` option.

exports.name: zoneOffsetMinutes
exports.description: `zone`'s offset from UTC in minutes at the instant `at` (Asia/Kolkata = 330, America/New_York = -240 in summer). Reads the one zone core, `offsetMinutesAt` (zone.ts).

exports.name: zoneAbbreviation
exports.description: The zone's short name at an instant ("EDT", "GMT+5:30", "UTC+05:30" for a fixed offset): what a field shows beside a time and what tells a repeated hour's two passes apart.
exports.signature: (zone: string, epochMs: number, locale?: string) => string

exports.name: zoneCity
exports.description: The readable place of a zone: `New York` for `America/New_York`, `UTC` for `Etc/UTC`, `UTC+05:30` for a fixed offset.

exports.name: zoneLabel
exports.description: The city, region and names of `zone` in `locale`, with its offset at `at` (default now).
exports.signature: (zone: string, locale?: string, at?: Date) => ZoneInfo

exports.name: buildZoneIndex
exports.description: `zoneLabel` for every zone, sorted by offset then city — the order a zone list reads best in.
exports.signature: (zones: readonly string[], locale?: string, at?: Date) => ZoneInfo[]

exports.name: searchZones
exports.description:
The zones matching `query` — every whitespace-separated word must hit the id,
city, region, long name, abbreviation or (when it has a digit) an offset spelling. Case- and
accent-insensitive; an empty query returns `zones` unchanged.

exports.name: groupByRegion
exports.description: Buckets zones by region (alphabetical, `Other` last), keeping each bucket in the input order.

exports.name: zonedWallTimeToInstant
exports.description:
The instant at which the wall clock in `zone` reads `date` `hour`:`minute`,
through the one zone core (`zonedDateTimeToEpoch`, zone.ts): a wall time a
spring-forward gap skips moves forward by the gap, a repeated fall-back time
takes the earlier instant, unless `disambiguation` says otherwise.
exports.signature: (date: string, hour: number, minute: number, zone: string, disambiguation?: Disambiguation) => Date

exports.name: formatZoneTime
exports.description: The wall-clock time of `at` in `zone`, `"14:05"` style per `locale`. A fixed offset is formatted as UTC shifted by it (an engine without offset zones would throw).
exports.signature: (zone: string, at: Date, locale?: string, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) => string

exports.name: UTC_ZONE
exports.description: The identifier every engine accepts but `supportedValuesOf` may leave out.

exports.name: FALLBACK_TIME_ZONES
exports.description: Used when the engine lacks `Intl.supportedValuesOf` (Safari < 15.4, older Node): one or two zones per populated offset.

exports.name: LEGACY_ZONE_IDS
exports.description:
CLDR keeps some renamed zones under their old ids, so engines list and
resolve `Asia/Calcutta`, not `Asia/Kolkata`; users search for the current
name. Each pair is old → current IANA id.

exports.name: ZoneInfo
exports.description: Everything the picker shows or searches for one zone, computed for one instant.

exports.name: OTHER_REGION
exports.description: The region bucket used when an id has no `/` (`UTC`, `GMT`) or is under `Etc/`.

exports.name: ZoneGroup
exports.description: One region heading and its zones.

exports.name: fixedOffsetMinutes
exports.description: A fixed-offset zone's offset in minutes (`UTC+05:30` → 330, `-04:00` → -240); `null` for an IANA id or a malformed offset.

exports.name: normalizeTimeZone
exports.description:
The id a zone is stored and compared under: a fixed offset in any spelling
becomes `±HH:MM` (`UTC+05:30` → `+05:30`, `GMT-4` → `-04:00`); an IANA id is
kept as given (`canonicalZone` in timezone.ts renames legacy ids).

exports.name: wallClockAt
exports.description: The wall clock in `zone` at the instant `epochMs`.

exports.name: offsetMinutesAt
exports.description: `zone`'s offset from UTC in whole minutes at the instant `epochMs` (Asia/Kolkata 330, New York -300 in winter, -240 in summer).

exports.name: inspectWallTime
exports.description:
Every instant at which the wall clock in `zone` reads `wall`, without
choosing. Like Temporal's `getPossibleInstantsFor`: the offsets a day before
and a day after bracket any change, and each one that reads back as `wall`
is an answer. A picker uses it to warn "this time happens twice".

exports.name: wallClockToEpoch
exports.description:
The instant at which the wall clock in `zone` reads `wall`, in epoch
milliseconds; `disambiguation` picks one when DST skips or repeats it (see
the file header). The ONE conversion: every kit's zoned-to-instant helper calls it.
exports.signature: (wall: WallClockInput, zone: string, disambiguation?: Disambiguation) => number

exports.name: formatWallClock
exports.description: `2026-07-01T09:30:00`, with `.250` only when the milliseconds are not zero (Temporal prints the same).

exports.name: formatInstant
exports.description: An instant as `2026-11-11T19:30:00Z` (no `.000`, unlike `Date#toISOString`).

exports.name: formatOffsetDateTime
exports.description: An instant as the wall time in `zone` with that moment's offset: `2026-07-01T09:30:00-04:00` (the form kit's stored date-time).

exports.name: formatZoned
exports.description: An instant in `zone` as RFC 9557: `2026-11-11T14:30:00-05:00[America/New_York]`.

exports.name: parseDateTime
exports.description: Splits an ISO date-time (`2026-07-01T09:30`, `…:00Z`, `…-04:00`, `…-04:00[America/New_York]`); `null` when malformed or impossible (Feb 30, 24:00).

exports.name: parseToEpoch
exports.description:
Any stored date-time string to epoch milliseconds; `null` when it cannot
name one instant. An offset (`Z`, `-04:00`) is exact. With a zone too, the
offset must be one the zone uses at that instant (Temporal's `offset:
"reject"`). A zone and no offset is resolved with `disambiguation`, and a
floating wall time needs `options.timeZone`. A `reject` refusal or an
unknown zone also gives `null`.

exports.name: zonedDateTimeToEpoch
exports.description: A plain date and a time of day in `zone` to epoch milliseconds: `zonedDateTimeToEpoch("2026-03-08", 150, "America/New_York")` is 03:30 EDT. `minutes` may pass 1440 (the next day). `NaN` for a malformed date.
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate, minutes: number, zone: string, disambiguation?: Disambiguation) => number

exports.name: isoDateAt
exports.description: The calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in `zone` at the instant `epochMs`.

exports.name: zonedDayTimes
exports.description:
The wall times `zone` really has on `date`, every `stepSeconds` on the wall
grid, in instant order: a spring-forward day leaves out
the times its gap skips (New York 2026-03-08 has no 02:00–02:59, so 23
hours of times), a fall-back day lists the repeated hour twice, earlier
pass first (New York 2026-11-01 has 01:00–01:59 at -04:00 and again at
-05:00, so 25 hours). A floating wall time has no zone and so every time
(`timeGrid`). The conversion is the one in this file.
exports.signature: (date: IsoDate, zone: string, stepSeconds: number, withSeconds?: boolean) => ZonedDayTime[]

exports.name: zonedDayHours
exports.description: How long `date` is in `zone`, in hours: 24 on most days, 23 on a spring-forward day, 25 on a fall-back one (30-minute zones give 23.5 or 24.5).

exports.name: toTemporalZoned
exports.description: An `IsoZoned` value as a `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` (the strings are the same, so this is `from`).
exports.signature: <Zoned, Instant>(value: IsoZoned, temporal: TemporalNamespace<Zoned, Instant>) => Zoned

exports.name: toTemporalInstant
exports.description: An `IsoInstant` (or an offset string) as a `Temporal.Instant`.
exports.signature: <Zoned, Instant>(value: IsoInstant | IsoOffsetDateTime, temporal: TemporalNamespace<Zoned, Instant>) => Instant

exports.name: fromTemporal
exports.description: A `Temporal.ZonedDateTime` or `Temporal.Instant` back to our string (`toString()` prints RFC 9557 or the `Z` form).

exports.name: DISAMBIGUATIONS
exports.description: How a wall time that a DST change skips or repeats picks its instant (Temporal's `disambiguation` option).

exports.name: Disambiguation
exports.description: One of `DISAMBIGUATIONS`: how a wall time a DST change skips or repeats picks its instant.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DISAMBIGUATION
exports.description: Temporal's default: forward through a gap, the earlier of two repeated instants.

exports.name: IsoInstant
exports.description: An exact instant in UTC, `2026-11-11T19:30:00Z` (`Temporal.Instant`'s string).

exports.name: IsoZoned
exports.description: A wall time with its offset and zone, RFC 9557: `2026-11-11T14:30:00-05:00[America/New_York]` (`Temporal.ZonedDateTime`'s string).

exports.name: IsoOffsetDateTime
exports.description: A wall time with its offset and no zone, `2026-07-01T09:30:00-04:00`: the form kit's stored date-time.

exports.name: WallClock
exports.description: The reading of a wall clock in some zone; `month` is 1–12, `hour` 0–23.

exports.name: WallClockInput
exports.description: A wall clock to convert: the time fields default to 0, and any field may overflow the way `Date.UTC` allows (minute 1440 is the next midnight).

exports.name: isFixedOffsetZone
exports.description: True for a fixed-offset zone in any accepted spelling.

exports.name: WallTimeKind
exports.description: What a wall time is in a zone: it happens once (`exact`), never (`gap`, skipped by a spring-forward change) or twice (`overlap`, a fall-back change).

exports.name: WallTimeResolution
exports.description: A wall time's possible instants: one when exact, two (earlier first) in an overlap, none in a gap.

exports.name: ZoneDisambiguationCode
exports.description: Why `reject` refused a wall time: a gap skipped it, or an overlap repeated it.

exports.name: ZoneDisambiguationError
exports.description: Thrown by `wallClockToEpoch` (and the helpers on it) under `disambiguation: "reject"` for a wall time that is not exactly one instant.

exports.name: ParsedDateTime
exports.description: The syntactic parts of an ISO date-time string, before any zone is consulted.

exports.name: ParseEpochOptions
exports.description: How `parseToEpoch` reads a string with no offset: the zone to read it in (when it names none) and how to pick in a DST gap or overlap.

exports.name: WallTimeOccurrence
exports.description: Which of a wall time's instants a listed time is: the only one, or the first or second pass of a fall-back hour.

exports.name: ZonedDayTime
exports.description: One wall time a zone has on a day, with its instant and offset.

exports.name: TemporalNamespace
exports.description: The slice of the Temporal namespace these helpers call; pass `globalThis.Temporal` where the engine has it (no polyfill dependency).

exports.name: stepNumber
exports.description:
The value one step up (`direction` 1) or down (-1), on the grid that starts at `min` (or 0): a value off the grid snaps to the next grid
point in that direction. From empty (null), up starts at `min` and down at `max` (else 0). Clamped, without float drift. It is the primitives'
`toValidatedNumber` (clamp, snap, float noise: the one stepping algorithm `useNumberField` runs) as a function of its own, kept for hosts.
exports.signature: (value: number | null, direction: 1 | -1, { step, amount, min, max }: NumberStepOptions) => number

exports.name: clampNumber
exports.description: `value` held inside `[min, max]` (either bound may be missing).
exports.signature: (value: number, min?: number, max?: number) => number

exports.name: decimalsOf
exports.description: Digits after the decimal point of a number, exponent notation included (1e-7 → 7).

exports.name: formatNumber
exports.description: `value` formatted for `locale` with `Intl.NumberFormat` options. The one number formatter (formatters are cached by locale and options).
exports.signature: (value: number, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions) => string

exports.name: formatPrecision
exports.description: The decimals the formatter shows for a value (percent adds two, since the value is a fraction).

exports.name: isPartialNumber
exports.description: True while `text` could still become a number in `locale` (empty, "-", "12,"), so a field can refuse other keystrokes.
exports.signature: (text: string, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: NumberFormatOptions) => boolean

exports.name: MINUS_SIGNS
exports.description: Characters people type for "minus": hyphen-minus, the Unicode minus sign, figure and en dashes, small and full-width hyphen-minus.

exports.name: numberFieldKeyAction
exports.description:
The spinbutton key table (WAI-ARIA spinbutton): ↑/↓ step, Shift+↑/↓ and
PageUp/PageDown take the large step, Home/End go to min/max. Returns null for
every other key, so typing stays the input's own.

exports.name: numberFormat
exports.description: A cached `Intl.NumberFormat` for one locale + options pair (a field formats on every keystroke).

exports.name: numberSymbols
exports.description: The group and decimal separators, affixes and digits for a locale + options pair (cached).

exports.name: parseNumber
exports.description:
Reads typed text in `locale` back into a number, or null when it is empty, a
lone sign or not a number. Group separators are dropped wherever they are, the
locale's decimal separator is the only one read as decimal, any minus variant
works, and currency, unit and percent affixes are ignored. With
`style: "percent"` the result is the shown number ÷ 100 ("15 %" → 0.15). No
rounding and no clamping; see {@link intlNumberFormatter} for those.
exports.signature: (text: string, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: NumberFormatOptions) => number | null

exports.name: roundTo
exports.description: `n` rounded to `digits` decimals, with the binary noise removed (0.1 + 0.2 → 0.3).

exports.name: NumberFieldKeyAction
exports.description: What a key does on a number spinbutton.

exports.name: NumberFormatOptions
exports.description: The Intl options a number field formats with (decimal, currency, percent, unit…).

exports.name: NumberSymbols
exports.description: The symbols one locale + options combination writes.

exports.name: NumberStepOptions
exports.description: Bounds and step for {@link stepNumber}.

exports.name: staticTimeZoneSource
exports.description: A fixed zone list, for a host that only offers its offices or its customers' regions.
exports.signature: (zones: readonly string[], detected?: string | null) => TimeZoneSource

exports.name: CalendarFormatter
exports.description: Every string a calendar shows or announces. Default: {@link intlCalendarFormatter} (Intl, any locale).

exports.name: intlCalendarFormatter
exports.description: The default formatter: Intl month captions, narrow weekday headers, locale numerals, full-date labels.

exports.name: TimeZoneSource
exports.description: Where the time-zone picker gets its zones. Default: {@link intlTimeZoneSource} (the engine's IANA list).

exports.name: intlTimeZoneSource
exports.description: The default zone source: `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")` (with a fallback list) and the host's zone.

exports.name: ColorSampler
exports.description:
Picks one colour from somewhere outside the picker: the screen (the browser's
EyeDropper, the default in `@kitora/pickers/dom`), an image, a brand palette
service. `sample` resolves to any colour string `parseColor` reads, or null
when the user cancelled.

exports.name: commitNumber
exports.description: A typed value through a formatter's parse, then held inside `[min, max]`; null stays null.
exports.signature: (text: string, formatter: NumberFormatter, locale: Intl.LocalesArgument | undefined, options: NumberFormatOptions | undefined, min?: number, max?: number) => number | null

exports.name: intlNumberFormatter
exports.description:
The default number formatter: Intl formatting, locale-aware parsing
({@link parseNumber}), rounded to the decimals the format shows, so the
committed value is exactly the one on screen.

exports.name: NumberFormatter
exports.description:
How a number field turns its value into text and typed text back into a
value. Default: {@link intlNumberFormatter} (Intl, any locale). Swap it for a
domain format (a "1.2k" shorthand, a duration "1h 30m", a fixed-point money
type) without touching the field.

exports.name: backspaceOtp
exports.description: Backspace at slot `index`: clears that slot when filled, else the one before it.

exports.name: insertOtp
exports.description:
Text arriving at slot `index` (one typed key, an autofill, or a paste): it
fills from that slot onward, overwriting, and focus moves past the last
character written. A value never has holes, so writing past the end appends.
exports.signature: (value: string, index: number, text: string, length: number, charset?: OtpCharset) => OtpEdit

exports.name: otpComplete
exports.description: Whether every slot is filled.

exports.name: OTP_PATTERNS
exports.description: The characters each charset accepts, one character per match.

exports.name: sanitizeOtp
exports.description: Keeps only accepted characters (upper-cased for alphanumeric), at most `length`.
exports.signature: (input: string, length: number, charset?: OtpCharset) => string

exports.name: OtpCharset
exports.description: Which characters a slot accepts in the pickers API.

exports.name: OtpEdit
exports.description: The result of an edit (`insertOtp`, `backspaceOtp`): the new value and the slot to focus.

exports.name: isEmojiData
exports.description: True when `source` is categories rather than a flat list.

exports.name: emojiDataOf
exports.description:
`source` as categories. A flat list becomes one unnamed category; a bare glyph takes its name and keywords from `known`
(the default set's by default), else its name is the glyph itself.

exports.name: emojiCount
exports.description: How many emoji the data holds (a glyph in two categories counts twice).

exports.name: isRichEmojiData
exports.description: Whether `data` is more than a quick set (several categories or more than {@link QUICK_EMOJI_LIMIT} emoji): it then gets search, the category bar and the preview by default.

exports.name: searchEmojiData
exports.description:
The emoji matching `query`, best match first, as one unnamed category (each glyph once, even when it sits in two
categories); an empty query returns `data` unchanged, and no match returns no category.

exports.name: glyphOf
exports.description: The glyph `item` shows in skin tone `skin`: its variant when it has skins, else its own glyph.

exports.name: skinOf
exports.description: The tone `glyph` is in for `item`: the index of its skin variant plus one, 0 for the default glyph or no match.

exports.name: hasEmojiSkins
exports.description: Whether any emoji in `data` has skin-tone variants (the skin-tone selector shows only then).

exports.name: emojiLookup
exports.description: Every glyph of `data` (each default glyph and each skin variant) to its item, for reading recents back.

exports.name: pushRecentEmoji
exports.description:
`recent` after picking `glyph`: it moves (or is added) to the front, any other tone of the same emoji is dropped, and
the list is cut to `limit`.
exports.signature: (recent: readonly string[], glyph: string, lookup: ReadonlyMap<string, EmojiItem>, limit?: number) => readonly string[]

exports.name: withRecentEmoji
exports.description:
`data` with the recently used emoji as a first category labelled `label` (none while `recent` is empty). Each glyph is
read back to its item (so it is named and toned like the rest); a glyph the data does not hold is named by itself.
exports.signature: (data: EmojiData, recent: readonly string[], label: string) => EmojiData

exports.name: EmojiItem
exports.description: One emoji: the glyph, the name screen readers say and search reads, and more words search finds it by.

exports.name: EmojiCategory
exports.description: A named group of emoji: a section of the grid and a button in the category bar.

exports.name: EmojiData
exports.description:
Every category the picker shows, in order. The kit ships no full emoji set: bring the data you use and map it. Most
emoji data packages publish one row per emoji with its group, name, keywords and skin variants; group the rows, and
keep the order the data gives (it is the order people expect).

exports.name: EmojiSource
exports.description: What `EmojiPicker`'s `emojis` takes: a flat list (glyphs or items, one unnamed category) or categories.

exports.name: DEFAULT_EMOJIS

exports.name: DatePicker
exports.description: One date picker for every mode, plus its parts for composing your own (see file header).

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value; `null` (or an empty range or list) is "nothing picked". Leave undefined for an uncontrolled picker.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value at first when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; leave undefined to let the picker open and close itself.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the picker starts open when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the picker opens or closes, with the new open state.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called on every committed change, with the new value and where it came from.

props.name: input
disabled
props.description: Whether the picker is disabled.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Range mode: the longest allowed range, in `lengthUnit`; `time-range`: minutes.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: minLength
props.description: Range mode: the shortest allowed range, in `lengthUnit` (days count both ends); `time-range`: minutes.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the value is shown but cannot be changed.

props.name: now
props.description: The current wall time for "Now"; default the host clock.

props.name: rules
props.description: Blocked days as data with reasons (`{ weekdays: [0, 6], reason: "Closed on weekends" }`, `{ dates }`, `{ ranges }`, `{ before }`, `{ after }`).

props.name: timeZone
props.description: The display zone (IANA id or fixed offset like `UTC+05:30`), controlled; see the file header. Setting any zone option makes `valueKind` default to `instant`.

props.name: calendar
props.description:
The calendar the day and week modes are drawn in:
`persian`, `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`, `japanese`, `hebrew` or
`gregory`; default the locale's `-u-ca-` extension, else Gregorian. The
value stays an ISO Gregorian date; the grid, its labels and the displayed
value are in the calendar, and the typed field keeps Gregorian numbers.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description: Force a 12- or 24-hour clock; default the locale's.

props.name: words
props.description: The grammar's words; the styled picker passes the `pickers` catalog's (English `PARSE_WORDS` otherwise).

props.name: confirm
props.description: Edit a draft and commit it with Apply (Cancel drops it); when false a pick commits.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 tag; default the browser's. Drives labels, the field order and the week start.

props.name: granularity
props.description: `day` (default) or a time precision: `single` and `range` then pick a date-time; the time modes default to `minute`.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description: Close when a pick completes the value; default true (multiple mode never closes on its own).

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Extra blocked days: `true` blocks, `{ reason }` blocks and says why (shown on the day, spoken, and in the field's error).

props.name: disablePast
props.description: Block every day before today (the display zone's today).

props.name: disableFuture
props.description: Block every day after today.

props.name: dayData
props.description: Async day data per visible month: labels under the days (prices), tones, blocked days with reasons.

props.name: dayDataKey
props.description: Changing it drops the day data cache and ignores responses still in flight.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: Override the locale's first day of the week.

props.name: weekNumbers
props.description: A week-number column in the day calendar: `true` / `"iso"` (ISO 8601 weeks) or `"locale"` (the locale's week-of-year).

props.name: trimMonthsToMax
props.description: Show no month wholly past `max` (the sheet's month scroller sets it, so it never runs past the last allowed month).

props.name: today
props.description: "Today" for highlighting, presets and the default month; default the host clock.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Months shown side by side in the day calendar.

props.name: anchorMonth
props.description:
With several months, which one opens on today (or on a preset that fits one
month) when nothing is picked: `last` (default) puts the past before it, as
an analytics range wants; `first` puts the future after it, as the bottom
sheet's vertical month scroller does.

props.name: pageBehavior
props.description: Page the day calendar by one month (`single`) or by every visible month (`page`).

props.name: outsideDays
props.description: The neighbouring months' days in the day calendar: `selectable`, `visible` (drawn, not pickable) or `hidden`.

props.name: fixedWeeks
props.description: Always draw six week rows so the surface never changes height; `false` drops rows outside the month.

props.name: lengthUnit
props.description: Range mode: count the range in `days` or `nights` (a 3-night stay spans 4 days; at least one night).

props.name: openEnded
props.description: Range modes: a value may keep one end (`{ start, end: null }`, "from 1 Jan"); default false.

props.name: allowsNonContiguousRanges
props.description: Range mode: a range may run across disabled days (both ends must be open); default false.

props.name: fields
props.description: Range modes: `split` (two fields, default for segments) or `one` (one field, default for `input="text"`).

props.name: maxSelected
props.description: Multiple mode: the most days that may be picked.

props.name: presets
props.description: Named ranges offered beside the calendar, in every date mode (`presetsForMode(mode)` gives the defaults); see the file header.

props.name: presetBehavior
props.description: What a preset pick does; default `accept` (pick and close), `stay` with `confirm`.

props.name: rollingPresets
props.description: `{ start, end }` modes: report a preset pick as `{ preset, start, end }` and re-resolve such a value against today.

props.name: compare
props.description: Offer a compare period of this kind (`DatePicker.Compare`); the user can switch it off or to the other kind.

props.name: compareEnabled
props.description: Whether the compare period is on (controlled).

props.name: defaultCompareEnabled
props.description: Whether the compare period starts on; default false.

props.name: onCompareChange
props.description: Called when the compare period is switched on or off or to the other kind, with whether it is on and its kind.

props.name: formatter
props.description: Every calendar label and announcement; default the Intl formatter.

props.name: naturalLanguage
props.description: With `input="text"`, read natural language ("next fri", "last 30 days") as well as formats. The segment field's paste never does.

props.name: quarterLabel
props.description: The quarter template for the text field (`Q{quarter} {year}`); the styled picker passes the catalog's.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: Minutes between times: the list's interval (default 30) and the minute column's step (default 1).

props.name: secondStep
props.description: Seconds between second-column values at `second` granularity; default 1.

props.name: timePanel
props.description: How the surface offers times: a `list` (default) or `columns` (default at `second` granularity).

props.name: minTime
props.description: The earliest time that may be picked: one time for every date, or per date (null while no date is picked).

props.name: maxTime
props.description: The latest time that may be picked (see `minTime`).

props.name: isTimeDisabled
props.description: Times that are taken or closed on a date (null in the time modes or before a date is picked).

props.name: timePresets
props.description: Named times in the panel (`DEFAULT_TIME_PRESETS`: Now, Noon, End of day).

props.name: overnight
props.description: `time-range` mode: an end before the start runs past midnight (a 22:00–06:00 shift); when false the end may not come first.

props.name: defaultTimeZone
props.description: The display zone when uncontrolled; default the host's zone (when another zone option asks for one).

props.name: onTimeZoneChange
props.description: Called when the display zone is switched, with the new zone.

props.name: zonePicker

exports.name: DatePickerProps
exports.description: Props of the ready-made `DatePicker` for one mode and granularity (the single-date picker's older props are a subset).

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value; `null` (or an empty range or list) is "nothing picked". Leave undefined for an uncontrolled picker.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value at first when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; leave undefined to let the picker open and close itself.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the picker starts open when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the picker opens or closes, with the new open state.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called on every committed change, with the new value and where it came from.

props.name: input
disabled
props.description: Whether the picker is disabled.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Range mode: the longest allowed range, in `lengthUnit`; `time-range`: minutes.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: minLength
props.description: Range mode: the shortest allowed range, in `lengthUnit` (days count both ends); `time-range`: minutes.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the value is shown but cannot be changed.

props.name: now
props.description: The current wall time for "Now"; default the host clock.

props.name: rules
props.description: Blocked days as data with reasons (`{ weekdays: [0, 6], reason: "Closed on weekends" }`, `{ dates }`, `{ ranges }`, `{ before }`, `{ after }`).

props.name: timeZone
props.description: The display zone (IANA id or fixed offset like `UTC+05:30`), controlled; see the file header. Setting any zone option makes `valueKind` default to `instant`.

props.name: calendar
props.description:
The calendar the day and week modes are drawn in:
`persian`, `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`, `japanese`, `hebrew` or
`gregory`; default the locale's `-u-ca-` extension, else Gregorian. The
value stays an ISO Gregorian date; the grid, its labels and the displayed
value are in the calendar, and the typed field keeps Gregorian numbers.

props.name: hourCycle
props.description: Force a 12- or 24-hour clock; default the locale's.

props.name: words
props.description: The grammar's words; the styled picker passes the `pickers` catalog's (English `PARSE_WORDS` otherwise).

props.name: confirm
props.description: Edit a draft and commit it with Apply (Cancel drops it); when false a pick commits.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 tag; default the browser's. Drives labels, the field order and the week start.

props.name: granularity
props.description: `day` (default) or a time precision: `single` and `range` then pick a date-time; the time modes default to `minute`.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description: Close when a pick completes the value; default true (multiple mode never closes on its own).

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Extra blocked days: `true` blocks, `{ reason }` blocks and says why (shown on the day, spoken, and in the field's error).

props.name: disablePast
props.description: Block every day before today (the display zone's today).

props.name: disableFuture
props.description: Block every day after today.

props.name: dayData
props.description: Async day data per visible month: labels under the days (prices), tones, blocked days with reasons.

props.name: dayDataKey
props.description: Changing it drops the day data cache and ignores responses still in flight.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: Override the locale's first day of the week.

props.name: weekNumbers
props.description: A week-number column in the day calendar: `true` / `"iso"` (ISO 8601 weeks) or `"locale"` (the locale's week-of-year).

props.name: trimMonthsToMax
props.description: Show no month wholly past `max` (the sheet's month scroller sets it, so it never runs past the last allowed month).

props.name: today
props.description: "Today" for highlighting, presets and the default month; default the host clock.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Months shown side by side in the day calendar.

props.name: anchorMonth
props.description:
With several months, which one opens on today (or on a preset that fits one
month) when nothing is picked: `last` (default) puts the past before it, as
an analytics range wants; `first` puts the future after it, as the bottom
sheet's vertical month scroller does.

props.name: pageBehavior
props.description: Page the day calendar by one month (`single`) or by every visible month (`page`).

props.name: outsideDays
props.description: The neighbouring months' days in the day calendar: `selectable`, `visible` (drawn, not pickable) or `hidden`.

props.name: fixedWeeks
props.description: Always draw six week rows so the surface never changes height; `false` drops rows outside the month.

props.name: lengthUnit
props.description: Range mode: count the range in `days` or `nights` (a 3-night stay spans 4 days; at least one night).

props.name: openEnded
props.description: Range modes: a value may keep one end (`{ start, end: null }`, "from 1 Jan"); default false.

props.name: allowsNonContiguousRanges
props.description: Range mode: a range may run across disabled days (both ends must be open); default false.

props.name: fields
props.description: Range modes: `split` (two fields, default for segments) or `one` (one field, default for `input="text"`).

props.name: maxSelected
props.description: Multiple mode: the most days that may be picked.

props.name: presets
props.description: Named ranges offered beside the calendar, in every date mode (`presetsForMode(mode)` gives the defaults); see the file header.

props.name: presetBehavior
props.description: What a preset pick does; default `accept` (pick and close), `stay` with `confirm`.

props.name: rollingPresets
props.description: `{ start, end }` modes: report a preset pick as `{ preset, start, end }` and re-resolve such a value against today.

props.name: compare
props.description: Offer a compare period of this kind (`DatePicker.Compare`); the user can switch it off or to the other kind.

props.name: compareEnabled
props.description: Whether the compare period is on (controlled).

props.name: defaultCompareEnabled
props.description: Whether the compare period starts on; default false.

props.name: onCompareChange
props.description: Called when the compare period is switched on or off or to the other kind, with whether it is on and its kind.

props.name: formatter
props.description: Every calendar label and announcement; default the Intl formatter.

props.name: naturalLanguage
props.description: With `input="text"`, read natural language ("next fri", "last 30 days") as well as formats. The segment field's paste never does.

props.name: quarterLabel
props.description: The quarter template for the text field (`Q{quarter} {year}`); the styled picker passes the catalog's.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: Minutes between times: the list's interval (default 30) and the minute column's step (default 1).

props.name: secondStep
props.description: Seconds between second-column values at `second` granularity; default 1.

props.name: timePanel
props.description: How the surface offers times: a `list` (default) or `columns` (default at `second` granularity).

props.name: minTime
props.description: The earliest time that may be picked: one time for every date, or per date (null while no date is picked).

props.name: maxTime
props.description: The latest time that may be picked (see `minTime`).

props.name: isTimeDisabled
props.description: Times that are taken or closed on a date (null in the time modes or before a date is picked).

props.name: timePresets
props.description: Named times in the panel (`DEFAULT_TIME_PRESETS`: Now, Noon, End of day).

props.name: overnight
props.description: `time-range` mode: an end before the start runs past midnight (a 22:00–06:00 shift); when false the end may not come first.

props.name: defaultTimeZone
props.description: The display zone when uncontrolled; default the host's zone (when another zone option asks for one).

props.name: onTimeZoneChange
props.description: Called when the display zone is switched, with the new zone.

props.name: zonePicker
props.description: A zone switch in the surface (`DatePicker.ZoneSelect`): `true` to switch, `"locked"` to show the zone fixed; default false.

props.name: valueKind
props.description: What a date-time value is: `floating`, `instant` (default with a zone) or `zoned` (RFC 9557).

props.name: disambiguation
props.description: How a wall time a DST change skips or repeats becomes an instant (Temporal's; default `compatible`). `reject` commits the typed time with `details.error` and a null value.

props.name: secondaryTimeZone
props.description: A second zone to show the picked time in ("9:00 AM New York = 7:30 PM Kolkata").

props.name: zoneDisplay
props.description: How the field shows the zone beside a date-time or time: `short` (default), `offset` or `none`.

props.name: timeZones
props.description: The zones the zone switch offers (IANA ids or fixed offsets); default every zone the engine knows.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The control's name; the range fields are "<label> start" / "<label> end".

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Id of the element that describes the field (a hint or an error).

props.name: id
props.description: Id for the field, so a `<label for>` can point at it.

props.name: name
props.description: Posts the value with a surrounding `<form>`: the ISO string, a list joined by commas, or a range as `start/end`.

props.name: startName
props.description: Range modes: post the start and the end as two fields instead.

props.name: endName
props.description: Range modes: the form name the end posts under (with `startName`).

props.name: required
props.description: A surrounding `<form>` refuses to submit until the value is whole (a range: both ends, unless `openEnded`); focus moves to the field.

props.name: form
props.description: The `form` the hidden inputs post into (a picker outside the `<form>` element).

props.name: invalid
props.description: Force the invalid look.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the read-only field and the button trigger while empty; default the catalog's "Pick a …".

props.name: side
props.description: Where the surface opens; default bottom, start.

props.name: align
props.description: How the surface lines up with the trigger along `side`; default start.

props.name: surface
props.description: The surface the panel opens on; default `auto` (see the file header).

props.name: sheetMonths
props.description: Months the sheet's vertical scroller shows first and adds each time it is scrolled to its end (day and week modes); default {@link SHEET_MONTHS}.

props.name: mode
props.description: Default `single`.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts (`DatePicker.Field`, `DatePicker.Surface`…) that read the picker state.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Show a clear (×) button when there is a value; default true.

props.name: footer
props.description: Extra content under the calendar (shortcuts like "Today"). Receives a function that sets the value and closes.

props.name: calendarClassNames
props.description: Per-part classes for the calendar in the surface.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the field (the inline panel when `surface` is `inline`).

exports.description: The emoji picker preset plus its parts for composing your own (see the file header).

props.name: trigger
props.description: The content of the button that opens the picker; defaults to a smiley icon (or, in value mode, the chosen emoji).

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's and the popover's accessible name; default the catalog's "Add reaction".

props.name: value
props.description:
Value mode ("pick an icon for this project"): the chosen emoji, controlled (null = none). The trigger shows it and the
grid marks it pressed. Value mode is on when any of `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `name` or `required` is set.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Value mode: the initial emoji when uncontrolled (null = none).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Value mode: called with the chosen glyph (toned, when a skin tone is set).

props.name: name
props.description: Value mode: posts the chosen glyph with a surrounding `<form>`; inside a `Field` the Field's `name` wins.

props.name: form
props.description: The `form` the value posts into (a picker outside the `<form>` element).

props.name: required
props.description: Value mode: a surrounding `<form>` refuses to submit while nothing is chosen; focus moves to the trigger.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the trigger is disabled (a disabled picker posts nothing).

props.name: invalid
props.description: Force the invalid look (a Field's error sets it too).

props.name: id
props.description: The trigger's id (a `<label htmlFor>` names it; inside a `Field` the Field's label does).

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled popover state.

props.description: Whether the popover starts open when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popover opens or closes, with the new state.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the trigger the popover opens on.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popover lines up with the trigger.

props.name: closeOnPick
props.description: Close the popover when an emoji is picked.

props.name: columns
props.description: Emoji per row of the grid.

props.name: recent
props.description:
The recently used emoji (glyphs, newest first), shown as a first "Recently used" category; the host keeps the list
(state, storage) and passes it back. Leave undefined for no recents.

props.name: skinTone
props.description: Controlled skin tone, 0 (default) to 5 (dark): every item with `skins` shows and is picked in it.

props.name: onPick
props.description: Called when an emoji is picked, with its glyph and the item.

props.name: emojis
props.description:
The emoji offered: a flat list of glyphs or items (one unnamed category), or categories (`EmojiData`). A bare glyph of
the default set takes its English name.

props.name: itemLabel
props.description: Each emoji button's accessible name; default the item's name ("thumbs up"). The chat kit passes `React ${emoji}`.

props.name: onRecentChange
props.description: Called after a pick with the new recent list: the picked glyph first, any other tone of it dropped, cut to `recentLimit`.

props.name: recentLimit
props.description: How many recently used emoji the list keeps.

props.name: defaultSkinTone
props.description: Initial skin tone when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSkinToneChange
props.description: Called when the skin tone changes, with the new tone.

props.name: search
props.description: Show the search box; default on for more than one category or more than 24 emoji.

props.name: preview
props.description: Show the preview footer; default on for more than one category or more than 24 emoji.

The 2D saturation (inline axis) × brightness (block axis) area for the current hue. One focusable
thumb with `role="slider"`: Left/Right change saturation, Up/Down brightness, and its value text
names both, so a screen reader hears the whole position on every step.

props.name: value
props.description: The current colour; the area shows its saturation and brightness on the plane of its hue.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called while dragging or on each key step, with the colour at the new saturation and brightness (hue and alpha kept).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name; default "Colour".

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the control ignores the pointer and the keys (the thumb leaves the tab order) and shows dimmed.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the root element.

exports.name: ColorPicker
exports.description: The inline colour panel (see file header), plus its parts for composing your own.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Presets under the inputs: hex strings or `{ value, label }`. Default {@link DEFAULT_COLOR_SWATCHES}; `[]` hides them.

props.name: swatchColumns
props.description: Swatches per row. Default 8.

props.name: formats
props.description: Formats the inputs offer. Default hex, rgb, hsl.

props.name: eyeDropper
props.description: Offer the sampler (eyedropper) where supported. Default true.

props.name: sampler
props.description: The sampler behind the eyedropper button; default the browser's EyeDropper.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether every part is disabled (a surrounding Field's `disabled` also disables it).

props.name: classNames
props.description: One class per part (merged after the part's own classes).
